skills/toil/ado.md

Work items, git repositories, pull requests and pipelines on Azure DevOps Server (on-premises), through its REST API with api-version=7.1. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: Azure DevOps Server 2022.1 or later (REST API 7.1). Requests send api-version=7.1 (7.1-preview.1 for connection data, 7.1-preview.4 for work item comments), which newer servers also accept. Azure DevOps Server 2022 RTM, 2020 and 2019 are out of scope: an older server’s “REST API version out of range” answer comes back as an error saying the server is too old for toil and naming 2022.1.

Credential

An Azure DevOps personal access token: in Azure DevOps, User settings → Personal access tokens → New Token. Give it the scopes the commands you’ll use need (Work Items, Code, Build; Read & write for the write commands). toil sends it as Authorization: Basic base64(":" + token), with an empty user name. There is no password or browser login.

In an Azure Pipelines job, the job’s own token, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN, is read when TOIL_ADO_PAT isn’t set (for the default connection, and before anything in the config file), so a pipeline step needs only TOIL_ADO_BASE_URL. Map it into the step’s environment (env: SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)).

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_ADO_BASE_URLyesServer root, e.g. https://ado.imagile.dev (keep any context path, such as /tfs)
patTOIL_ADO_PAT (or SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN)yesPersonal access token
collectionTOIL_ADO_COLLECTIONnoDefault collection, when --collection isn’t given
projectTOIL_ADO_PROJECTnoDefault team project, when --project isn’t given
repoTOIL_ADO_REPOnoDefault git repository, when --repo isn’t given
fieldAliasesTOIL_ADO_FIELD_ALIASESnoWork item field aliases as a JSON object, friendly name to reference name, e.g. {"storypoints": "Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.StoryPoints"}
discoveredFieldsTOIL_ADO_DISCOVERED_FIELDSnoFields an earlier discovery recorded; kept, not read
discoveredTypesTOIL_ADO_DISCOVERED_TYPESnoWork item types an earlier discovery recorded; kept, not read
writesTOIL_ADO_WRITESnotrue lets write commands run (with --allow-write)

Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell):

export TOIL_ADO_BASE_URL=https://ado.imagile.dev
export TOIL_ADO_PAT=<your personal access token>

Or ~/.toil/config.json, with collection, project and repo usually set once under defaults.ado:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "corp-ado": { "area": "ado", "baseUrl": "https://ado.imagile.dev", "writes": true }
  },
  "defaults": { "ado": { "connection": "corp-ado", "collection": "DefaultCollection", "project": "Imagile", "repo": "imagile-api" } }
}

The token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add corp-ado --area ado (or toil connections login corp-ado for an existing connection) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_ADO_PAT.

Where a command acts

--collection <name> (or its alias --organization <name>), --project <name> and --repo <name> are group flags, accepted before or after the command (toil ado --project Imagile work get --id 42). Without them, toil reads them from the first of the workspace’s remotes on the connection’s host, of any name, trying origin first (https://<host>[/tfs]/<collection>/<project>/_git/<repo>, or the _ssh forms with ssh://git@<host> or git@<host>:), then the connection’s collection, project and repo settings. --collection beats --organization, which beats the remote and the settings. An ssh:// remote with no user, an HTTPS remote with a user name, and the short <collection>/_git/<project> form aren’t read correctly. meta.context says where each came from.

Every command needs a collection and a project, even the ones that don’t use them (whoami, project list-collections), and fails with “Could not determine Azure DevOps collection” (or project) when either is missing. Every repo command except list and create also needs a repo.

Ids are read as whole numbers from the start of the text: 12abc is 12, and abc is sent as NaN.

Commands

Server and projects:

  • whoami, connection-data: The collection’s connection data: the authenticated user (authenticatedUser.id is the identity id the vote commands use), the instance and the deployment. The two return the same thing.
  • project list-collections: The server’s project collections.
  • project list: Every team project in the collection.
  • project get: One team project by --name.

Work items (--id <n>):

  • work get: A work item with every field and relation.
  • work create: Create one (--type, --title, --description, --assignee, --priority, --field name=value repeatable, --input-file). --parent <id> adds a parent link afterwards; the result is the item as created, and a failed link is only an ADO_PARENT_LINK_FAILED warning, with the item already created.
  • work update: Set fields (--field name=value repeatable, or --input-file).
  • work transition: Set --state.
  • work assign: Assign --to a display name or email.
  • work link: Link --id to --to, --type related (default), parent, child, duplicate, duplicate-of, or a raw relation name.
  • work search: Run --wiql; returns the matching ids and urls, not their fields. --updated-since <iso> keeps only items changed at or after that instant: a date (2026-10-01, UTC midnight) or a date-time with its zone (2026-10-01T09:00:00Z). toil ANDs [System.ChangedDate] >= '<instant>' onto the query’s own WHERE, in parentheses so an OR keeps its meaning, and asks the server for time precision. Time precision applies to the whole query, so with --updated-since an = on a date field ([System.CreatedDate] = @Today) matches one exact instant, not a day; write date conditions with >= and < instead. It and --limit work on flat queries (FROM WorkItems) only; a link query is refused. With --limit, each page runs the query again, so an item changed in between can move. A query returns at most 20,000 items, so a page can’t end past that.
  • work get-batch --id <n> --id <n>: Several work items through the batch endpoint, 200 ids per request, at most 1,000 per call. Returns { count, value, missing }: value holds the items found in the order asked, with every field and relation, or only --fields System.Title,System.State; missing lists each id that doesn’t exist or the token can’t see, with an ADO_WORK_ITEMS_MISSING warning.
  • work revisions --id <n>: Every revision of a work item, oldest first; each is the whole item as it stood after that change, so neighbours show what changed and when.
  • work list-comments, work add-comment (--body): Comments; listing reads the first page only.
  • work add-tag, work remove-tag: --tags a;b or a,b, matched ignoring case. The tag list is read and written back, with no revision check.
  • work list-attachments: The attached files (id, name, url, size, dates).
  • work add-attachment: Upload --file (a path in the workspace), then link it (--comment optional). Returns the uploaded attachment’s { id, url }. If the link fails, the upload stays on the server.
  • work download-attachment: Save --attachment-id to --dir (default .toil) in the workspace; returns { saved, name, size }. It never overwrites a file. The token only goes to the configured host: an attachment URL naming another host is fetched from the configured one, with an ADO_ATTACHMENT_HOST warning.
  • work list-areas, work list-iterations: The area or iteration tree, --depth (default 10).
  • work types: The work item types with their states and required fields.
  • work list-states: The states of --type.
  • work fields: The collection’s fields, or with --type a type’s (those have no type or readOnly); --custom-only drops System.* and Microsoft.VSTS.*.
  • work schema: The --input-file JSON schema and an example; --example-only returns just the example as data. Needs no connection.

work types and work fields have no --save; passing it is an unknown option. The aliases --save would store are the built-in ones below, which apply anyway. --discover is accepted and changes nothing.

Field names in --field and --input-file resolve through the connection’s fieldAliases, then the built-in aliases (title, state, description, priority, storypoints, acceptancecriteria, reprosteps and others), matched ignoring case, spaces and dashes; anything else is sent as a reference name (MyOrg.Team). To add your own alias, set fieldAliases as a JSON object: toil connections add <name> --area ado asks for it when setting up a connection; on one that exists, add "fieldAliases": { "effortdays": "MyOrg.EffortDays" } to it in ~/.toil/config.json, or set TOIL_ADO_FIELD_ALIASES (or TOIL_CONN_<NAME>_FIELD_ALIASES) to the JSON. An --input-file is { "type": "Bug", "fields": { "Title": "...", "Description": "@desc.html" } }: a value starting with @ is read from that file. Flags win over the file, with an ADO_INPUT_OVERRIDDEN warning naming the keys.

Repositories and pull requests:

  • repo list, repo create (--name), repo get: Repositories in the project.
  • repo list-prs: Every pull request, --state active (default), abandoned, completed or all. --creator and --reviewer are sent as identity id filters, so pass an id (from whoami), not an alias. --created-after and --created-before take ISO 8601 dates; a date alone is UTC midnight, a date-time without a zone is local time.
  • repo get-pr: One by --id.
  • repo create-pr: --title, --source, --target (default main), --description, --reviewers <id,id> (identity ids), --draft. Give branch names without refs/heads/, which toil adds (a full ref gets it twice).
  • repo update-pr: --title, --description, --reviewers, --draft true|false, in one PATCH.
  • repo merge-pr: Ask the server to complete it, --strategy noFastForward (default), squash, rebase or rebaseMerge, --delete-source. Completion is asynchronous; check data.status.
  • repo abandon-pr: Abandon it.
  • repo list-comments --pr <n>: Every comment of every thread, oldest first, with threadId and threadContext (null for a general comment); system comments included. --inline-only or --general-only narrows it.
  • repo add-comment, repo add-inline-comment (--file /src/a.ts --line 12, --line-type left|right, default right), repo reply-comment --thread-id, repo resolve-comment --thread-id (status fixed).
  • repo delete-comment --thread-id --comment-id: Returns { "deleted": true }. CLI only: deletes are never exposed through MCP.
  • repo list-files --pr <n>: Changed files of the latest iteration, at most 100.
  • repo diff --pr <n>: Changed files between the last merge commits, at most 100; --path keeps one file (a leading / is added).
  • repo get-build-status --commit <sha>: Statuses posted to a commit.
  • repo list-reviewers --pr <n>: Reviewers and their votes.
  • repo list-default-reviewers: Required reviewers policies covering the repository.
  • repo approve, repo unapprove, repo wait-for-author (--pr <n>): Vote 10, 0 or -5 as the token’s own user.
  • repo list-builds --pr <n>: Builds of the pull request’s source branch (not of its merge ref).

Pipelines:

  • pipeline list, pipeline get --id: Pipelines (build definitions).
  • pipeline run --id: Queue a run, --branch (a short name gets refs/heads/), --parameter k=v repeatable. --wait polls every --poll seconds (10) for up to --timeout seconds (600). A result other than succeeded still returns the build, with an ADO_BUILD_NOT_SUCCEEDED warning, and the CLI exits 1. The command’s own time limit is 11 minutes, so a longer --timeout also needs TOIL_TIMEOUT_MS.
  • pipeline list-runs: Runs, --definition <id> or --name <pipeline>, --branch (as given, e.g. refs/heads/main), --status, --top (default 50; --top 0 lists every run).
  • pipeline get-run --id, pipeline cancel-run --id: One run; cancel it.
  • pipeline logs --build-id <n> (or --id): The run’s logs; with --log-id, that log’s text as { "log": "..." }.

Paging: project list, pipeline list, pipeline list-runs, repo list-prs, repo list-builds, work search and work revisions return the whole list by default. With --limit <n> they return at most that many and set meta.page.nextCursor; pass it back as --cursor, with the same --limit, for the next page, until it’s null. pipeline list-runs takes --limit or --top, not both. Every list except work search (one request) reads page by page and stops with an HTTP error after 1,000 pages, naming the list.

Write commands need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write on the call.

toil ado --collection DefaultCollection --project Imagile work get --id 42
toil ado work create --type Bug --title "Login broken" --field "Story Points=3" --allow-write
toil ado --repo imagile-api repo list-prs --state all
toil ado work search --wiql "SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems" --updated-since 2026-10-01 --limit 200
toil ado work get-batch --id 42 --id 7 --fields System.Title,System.State
toil ado pipeline run --id 5 --branch main --wait --allow-write

Checking a dossier

check-dossier checks the call’s dossier against the server: each team project it names (project, per repo or not, and projects) exists in its collection, and each repository (repo) in its project. The collection is the section’s collection, else --collection or the connection’s; a value with no collection anywhere is INVALID_INPUT. It’s toil ado check-dossier (--dossier <name|file>, or the dossier the folder resolves to), and it returns { dossier, connection, env, ok, checked, checks, unchecked }, one check per value with its key path. The CLI exits 1 when one is missing. A failure other than not-found (a bad token, an unreachable host) fails the command. Read only.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Azure DevOps Server root, e.g. https://ado.imagile.dev (keep any /tfs prefix)

    TOIL_ADO_BASE_URL

  • pat required secret

    Personal access token

    TOIL_ADO_PAT orSYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN

  • collection

    Default collection, when --collection isn't given

    TOIL_ADO_COLLECTION

  • project

    Default team project, when --project isn't given

    TOIL_ADO_PROJECT

  • repo

    Default git repository, when --repo isn't given

    TOIL_ADO_REPO

  • fieldAliases

    Work item field aliases, friendly name to reference name (e.g. {"storypoints": "Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.StoryPoints"})

    TOIL_ADO_FIELD_ALIASES

  • discoveredFields

    Work item fields recorded by an earlier discovery; kept, not read

    TOIL_ADO_DISCOVERED_FIELDS

  • discoveredTypes

    Work item types recorded by an earlier discovery; kept, not read

    TOIL_ADO_DISCOVERED_TYPES
